:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='55%'}

Remember this one?

::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-hospital" align="center" icon-size="1.5em"}
What if we opened a new site here?

:::

## Flavours of Location Problem

Many geographic problems come down to one of these three things:

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='33%'}

::: {.value-box value="Expansion"  icon-position="top" align="center" icon="fa-solid fa-circle-plus"}
"I need to **add** a site"

*Where should our new community diagnostic centre go?*

:::

:::

::: {.column width='33%'}

::: {.value-box value="Consolidation" icon-position="top" align="center" icon="fa-solid fa-circle-minus"}

I need to **remove** a site

*Which of our sites do we close when the estate has to shrink?*

:::

:::

::: {.column width='33%' icon-position="top" align="center" icon="fa-brands fa-connectdevelop"}

::: {.value-box value="Network Design"}

I need to work out where to put a *load* of sites where none currently 'exist'

*Where do all the vaccination centres go?*
:::

:::

::::


## Why can't we just eyeball it?

Let's imagine you've got 15 candidate sites, and you need to open some.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="15" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 1 site.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="105" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 2 sites.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="455" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 3 sites.
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="1365" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 4 sites.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="3003" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 5 sites.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='33%'}
::: {.value-box value="5005" fragment="fade-in"}
Options to weigh up when opening 6 sites.
:::
:::

::::

::: {.fragment}
**Location Optimization** is a branch of operational research that allows us to evaluate and rank these combinations
:::


## Best at what?

Before it can rank anything, the model has to be told what "best" means.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-clock-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
The shortest **average journey**?
:::
:::

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-people-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
The most people **within 30 minutes**?
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-bar-chart-fill" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
The best access for the **most deprived** areas?
:::
:::

::: {.column width='50%'}
::: {.value-box icon="bi bi-sliders" fragment="fade-in" icon-position="left"}
The most **even workload** across sites?
:::
:::

::::

::: {.fragment}

The model doesn't decide which of these matters. [**You**]{style="color:yellow"} do.

:::


## Decision *Support*, not Decisions

Like most good operational research, this should be treated as *decision support*

It's not telling you the one 'right' answer

It's just more robust evidence to add to

- system knowledge
- patient feedback
- what's actually deliverable

::: {.value-box fragment="fade-in"}

The best site on paper might be the one you can't build on.

And once a service opens, demand you never knew about can appear.

:::
